issue.title: TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON and FuzzMarshalRaw are red on Go 1.27: encoding/json escapes U+2028/2029 with SetEscapeHTML(false) now
issue.body:
On go1.27.3 (linux/amd64, a WSL2 dev box), on current main:

    go test -tags nogui -run 'TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON|FuzzMarshalRaw' ./internal/gateway/

is red:

    escape false:
         marshalRaw   "[\"line\u2028sep\u2029\"]"
         encoding/json "[\"line\\u2028sep\\u2029\"]"

encoding/json's Encoder changed in Go 1.27: with SetEscapeHTML(false) it now
escapes U+2028 and U+2029 (it left them raw through 1.26, which is what
fastjson's marshalRaw matches and documents at internal/gateway/fastjson.go:1321
"U+2028, U+2029 escaped when escapeHTML, as json.Marshal writes them"). A
one-liner shows it on 1.27.3:

    enc := json.NewEncoder(&b); enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
    enc.Encode([]any{"line\u2028sep\u2029", nil})
    // "[\"line\\u2028sep\\u2029\",null]"  — escaped

CI stays green (it runs 1.26.x), so this only bites local runs on Go 1.27.
FuzzMarshalRaw fails the same way on seed #7.

The call is magpie's: keep fastjson's (json/v2-aligned) raw behavior and pin
the divergence in the test per Go version, or escape with 1.27 when not
escaping HTML to keep the equivalence.

comments.body:
Patch: [fix/3547-marshalraw-go127-line-separators](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3547-marshalraw-go127-line-separators), current head [0864a99ae42d47d1a3f4f4e76b5330fecf3759af](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/0864a99ae42d47d1a3f4f4e76b5330fecf3759af).

Correction to the first version: comparison now escapes actual U+2028/U+2029 characters on both sides instead of unescaping backslash-u sequences. This preserves literal backslash-u text. An exact-byte regression distinguishes the actual separators from literal escapes. go/version replaces the handwritten version parser. marshalRaw production bytes are unchanged.

Reproduced the original test and fuzz-seed failures on Go 1.27.3. TestMarshalRaw and FuzzMarshalRaw seed tests pass with -race (1.341s); vet and go build ./... pass.

Full gateway suite: the combined tree at upstream a41d0d50 with this fix, #3549, #3680 and the existing #3280 Claude harness fix passed (324.723s). The independent branch has those other known package-test failures; the combination result is not a standalone suite pass. Go 1.26 was not run in this session.

issue.title: [feat] Settings › Observability: Test the OTLP connection (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## The problem In Settings › Observability, once the OTLP endpoint and headers are filled in, nothing says whether they work. A wrong key, a host without `/api/public/otel`, or `http://` where the collector redirects to `https://` all end the same way: `otel: traces export failed; batch dropped` in the log, and nothing in the collector. The only check is to send real traffic and go look in Langfuse. An SSH or database client has a Test connection button for this; Observability has none. ## What the branch does **Test connection**, a row under OTLP headers on the Collector connection card, with a Test button. It sends an **empty export** (`{"resourceSpans":[]}`, and `{"resourceMetrics":[]}` when Export metrics is on), so the collector checks the endpoint and headers and records nothing. The lines under the row say what it met: | Answer | What the row says | | --- | --- | | 2xx | Works: `` took a test export in N ms | | 401 / 403 | `` refused the headers (401): check the keys, and that they are for this host, then *The collector says: …* | | 404 / 405, or a web page answering | No collector answers at `` (404): check the endpoint's path. Langfuse's ends in /api/public/otel | | 3xx | `` redirects to `
`, and exports don't follow redirects: use that address as the endpoint | | other status | `` answered 503, then the collector's own message | | no connection | Couldn't reach ``: dial tcp: lookup …: no such host | | no answer in 3s | `` didn't answer within 3 seconds, so an export there would be dropped | Every string is in zh, zh-TW, ja and de. ## How it works, and why it says what an export would meet - `otlp.Check` sends the empty export **by the exporter's own code**. `otelClient` (the proxy in force, 3s, no redirect followed), `signalURL` and `exportRequest` were pulled out of `send` and are shared with it; `send`'s behaviour is unchanged, and the existing exporter tests pass as they were. - `POST /api/otel/test` tries `settings.OTelExport()`: the saved settings under any `MAGPIE_OTEL_*`, which is what the exporter sends to, with export **on or off** (so it can be tried before turning export on). It **takes no endpoint or headers from the request**, so the route can't be used to send the saved credentials anywhere else. The page waits for a field's pending save (`prefsQueue`) before it asks, so a value typed and not yet saved is the one tested. - Header values (whole, each long word, and Basic's decoded user and password) are taken out of anything the collector says back. HTML answers are never shown. - An unreadable `settings.json` is said as such, not as "no endpoint" (`settings.LoadChecked` first). - No new destination: the request goes only to the collector the user configured, with the headers they configured for it. ## Checked against the real Langfuse Cloud (US) The built binary (`magpie web`, `-tags nogui`) in a sandbox HOME, with its own gateway port, `MAGPIE_NO_ACCOUNTS=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, never the running magpie: | Saved settings | `POST /api/otel/test` answered | | --- | --- | | correct keys, export Off | `200`, "Works" in ~260 ms | | wrong secret key | `401` auth, "Invalid credentials. Confirm that you've configured the correct host." | | host without `/api/public/otel` | `404` path (Langfuse's HTML 404 page, not shown) | | `http://` instead of `https://` | `301` redirect, suggests `https://us.cloud.langfuse.com:443/api/public/otel`; saving that address → `200` | | Export metrics on | traces `200`, metrics `200` | | a host that doesn't resolve | network, "dial tcp: lookup …: no such host" | | nothing saved | 400 "Set the OTLP endpoint first" | - **The collector records nothing:** after three Tests, Langfuse's `GET /api/public/v2/observations` for that window returned 0 observations, while the same query over the hours before returns the project's real gateway traces. - **The secret never comes back:** neither the secret key nor its base64 appears in any answer. - **The real page:** driven in Chromium against the sandbox, with a wrong header typed (not saved) and Test clicked: the field was saved first, then tested, and the 401 and Langfuse's message showed. Screenshots below. ## The branch - Diff against main: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...0xJchen:magpie:otel-test-connection - One commit, rebased on main `7499ebb5`: https://github.com/0xJchen/magpie/commit/7d9f65d30672 ```sh git fetch https://github.com/0xJchen/magpie.git otel-test-connection git cherry-pick 7d9f65d30672 ``` 14 files, +933 −15: `internal/otlp/check.go` (new), `internal/otlp/otel.go` (helpers shared with `send`), `internal/gui/oteltest.go` (new route), `internal/gui/api.go` (registration), `app.js` / `app.css` / `i18n.js` (the row), tests, `docs/reference.md` (OTLP export) and `docs/subsystems/plugin-runtime.md` (`plugins/otel`). **app.js size:** the row adds 2,769 bytes to app.js, and `TestCoreScriptBudget`'s two budgets are raised by exactly that, with the reason in their comments, as for other Settings rows. If you'd rather Observability's section moved into `plugins/otel`'s own client files first, I can do that as a separate commit. ## What was run (at 7d9f65d30, on main 7499ebb5) Go under a sandbox HOME, on go1.26.8 (go.mod's and CI's): - `gofmt -l` on the changed files prints nothing. `go vet ./...` for darwin, `GOOS=linux -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows`, plus the three builds: ok. - **New tests:** `TestCheck*` (5, `-race`) and `TestOTelTest*` (3) pass. `otel-check.test.cjs` passes 12 of 12 in Chromium and in WebKit, in every language, at 1100 and 420 px wide. - **Each guarantee broken by hand,** with its test red, then restored: - headers dropped; - redirects followed; - proxy ignored; - a URL built apart from `signalURL`; - metrics skipped; - a 2xx web page taken as working; - header values not scrubbed; - a timeout read as a network fault; - `LoadChecked` dropped; - the request's endpoint taken; - `MAGPIE_OTEL_*` ignored; - the page not waiting for a pending save; - an answer kept after the endpoint changes; - the collector's words dropped; - the page as it is on main. - **`go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`:** 70 packages ok. The one red is `internal/provider`, #3632, which is red the same on main's own CI. On go1.27.2, four `internal/gateway` tests are red on main too and green on 1.26.8: #3547 (two tests), #3549, and `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`, which is unfiled. - **The whole GUI suite** (896 files, both engines, at c0985122 + this change; 7499ebb5 touches no GUI file): 27 files had a red. Each was run on main beside this branch under the same load, and none is red here and green on main. Filed: #3497, #2572, #3479, #3403, #3402, #3079, #3410, #3411, #3637, #3408, #3096, #3412, #3409, #3413, #3414, #2549, #2399, #3415, #1876. Unfiled but red on main: `quota-refresh-order` (since 09c0a844), `search-first`, `skill-gone`. Five were red under load only. - **Since then:** main moved to 19253f67 (the Routing plugin's own script). The commit applies onto it without conflict. The full record is in the commit body. ## Not tried - **Other collectors:** an OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb and self-hosted Langfuse weren't tried, only Langfuse Cloud (US). A collector that accepts an export without checking headers passes the Test. A 200 means the collector took the export, not that it keeps that signal: Langfuse answers 200 on `/v1/metrics` too, while the Export metrics row says to leave metrics off for it. - **Linux and Windows:** only vetted and built (`GOOS=linux`, `GOOS=windows`), not run. The change is an HTTP request and a Settings row, with nothing per-OS. - **The desktop window:** the page was tested in Playwright's Chromium and WebKit and in `magpie web`, not in the macOS app's own WebKit window.

issue.title: gui tests: quota-refresh-order is red on main since 09c0a844: its sandbox has no quotasKept

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`internal/gui/tests/quota-refresh-order.test.cjs` fails 9 of 9 on main c158b0439, in about 1 ms each, before it tests anything:

```
ReferenceError: quotasKept is not defined
```

Run at c158b0439 with nothing else changed (it needs no browser, so the engine and the machine's load don't matter):

```sh
node --test internal/gui/tests/quota-refresh-order.test.cjs
```

**Cause:** 09c0a844 ("gui: the tray panel draws its last allowances at once…", #3160, #3134) added a top-level `let quotasKept = false;` to app.js, and the quota-loading code it changed now reads and writes it (`quotasKept = true` on a kept reading, `quotasKept = reading = false` on a reply or a failure). The test copies selected functions out of app.js into a sandbox of its own, and that sandbox declares no `quotasKept`, so the first call into the loader throws. Its nine cases haven't tested the refresh order since that commit. They cover a background read started before or during a card refresh, crossed full-list replies, a renamed card, and the rest. CI doesn't run the GUI suite, so nothing showed it.

**Likely fix:** give the test's sandbox `quotasKept`, the way it gives the loader's other top-level state. Then check that each case still goes red when the order it guards is broken by hand.

Found while running the whole GUI suite for #3678; that branch doesn't touch the quota code.

issue.title: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback is red on Go 1.27: its probe reuses a kept-alive connection after the WSL listener closes

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (`internal/gateway/wsl_test.go`) fails 3 of 3 on main c158b0439 with go1.27.2 darwin/arm64, and passes 3 of 3 there with go1.26.8 (go.mod's, CI's). I couldn't find it filed. #3547 and #3549 are the other Go 1.27 reds from the same run.

```
--- FAIL: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback (10.03s)
    wsl_test.go:165: WSL network gone: http://[::1]:58208/ answers = true
```

Run, in a sandbox HOME at c158b0439 with nothing else changed:

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local   go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # go1.27.2: FAIL
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # ok
```

**Likely cause, checked once:** `answers()` makes a new `http.Client` with no Transport, so every probe goes through `http.DefaultTransport` and its pool of kept-alive connections. After "WSL network up", the pool holds a connection to `[::1]:port`. Closing the WSL listener doesn't close connections it has already accepted, so the "WSL network gone" probe is answered over that connection, and on Go 1.27 it holds for the whole 10s wait. With only the probe changed to `&http.Client{Timeout: time.Second, Transport: &http.Transport{DisableKeepAlives: true}}`, the test passes 3 of 3 on go1.27.2. Not checked: what changed between 1.26 and 1.27 to make the old connection last the wait.

issue.title: [bug] sessions: a Claude Code fork subagent's copy of its parent's reply is counted twice (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Branch: [fish2lab/magpie `sessions-claude-fork-copy`](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/tree/sessions-claude-fork-copy), one commit, [df11f97](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/commit/df11f97d0e16279d889b0f0da8a353b6d903661d), on origin/main 7d075df. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie sessions-claude-fork-copy && git cherry-pick df11f97
```

## What's wrong

A Claude Code fork subagent's transcript (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, here from Claude Code 2.1.302) opens with a `fork-context-ref` line. Next comes a copy of the parent's reply that started the fork, with the same `message.id` and `requestId`, now marked `isSidechain: true` with the fork's `agentId`. Then comes the fork's own prompt. The parent's main file already counts that reply, and the sessions reader dedupes calls only within a file. So `magpie sessions` and the stats count the reply once more for every fork.

## The fix

Subsystem: sessions (`internal/sessions`, the Claude Code reader). No subsystem reference documents how Claude transcripts are counted, so no page changes.

- Trigger: a `fork-context-ref` line. The reader sets `state.ForkHead` and skips assistant lines until the file's first user line. It does this both in the fast path (`claudeLine`) and in the full parse (`claudeFull`). The first user line clears the flag, and everything after it is counted as before.
- Before: the copied reply counted once in the parent's file and again in each fork's file. After: it counts once, in the parent's file.
- State: `ForkHead` is kept in the parse cache (`fork_head`), so a read that resumes inside the head still skips. `cacheVersion` goes from 22 to 23, so files parsed before are read again.
- Files without a `fork-context-ref` line read as before. These include ordinary subagents, workflow agents and main transcripts.

## Verification

Run at df11f97 (on origin/main 7d075df), go1.27.3 darwin/arm64:

- `gofmt -l` is clean.
- Vet is clean: `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.
- Builds are ok: `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows go build`.
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` in a sandbox HOME with Go's caches pinned: 69 packages ok, including `internal/sessions` (ok, 73s). A few packages are red, and they are red in the same way on origin/main 7d075df without this change:
  - `internal/provider`: #3632 (ok in 71s with `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` skipped)
  - `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw` (#3547), `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (#3549), `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (#3680)
  - `internal/plugin`: `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207)
- Broken by hand: I put the old `claude.go` and `sessions.go` back and kept the new test. `TestClaudeForkSubagentCountsParentReplyOnce` then fails with `session: {Input:250 Output:25 CacheRead:30 ...}, want {Input:150 Output:15 CacheRead:20 ...}`. With the change restored, it passes.

I also checked against real data. I copied one real session (its main file and its one fork) into a sandbox, with HOME, the XDG dirs and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` all pointing there, and ran `magpie sessions --json` with binaries built from origin/main and from this branch:

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| input | 238 | 236 |
| output | 153,562 | 150,944 |
| cache read | 24,171,440 | 24,041,229 |
| cache write | 388,781 | 387,933 |

The branch's numbers equal that session's calls deduped by `message.id` + `requestId` across all of its files, as counted by an independent reader, [git-tab](https://github.com/fish2lab/git-tab)'s Claude Code adapter.

Not tried:

- Cowork transcripts, which use the same reader.
- Running on Linux or Windows; only the GOOS vet and builds above were run. The change has no platform code.

## Found while checking, not changed here

I compared 115 sessions from the last 30 days against git-tab, and 100 matched to the cent. Three other differences come from magpie behavior I left alone. I can open a separate issue for any of them if useful:

- `sessions` and the stats price each model's total at its base tier (`p.At(0)` in `sessions.go` and `stats.go`). So Claude Haiku 5.5's rate for prompts above 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 per MTok, against $0.10/$0.50) is never applied. One pi session on Haiku 5.5 had identical tokens on both sides. It cost $0.12 in magpie, against $0.52 when each request is priced at its tier.
- DeepSeek's peak-hour price is not applied. It is 2× on weekdays 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 Beijing time ([pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing)). Two pi sessions on deepseek-flash that ran entirely in peak hours came out at half their price.
- A forked or resumed Claude Code session copies its parent's history into a new main file under a new `sessionId`. Per-session totals then count the copied calls in both sessions. In one fork the copies made up 95% of its listed cost: $6.62 listed, against $0.31 for its own calls.

issue.title: Chat passthrough for a "deepseek"-named upstream: injected `reasoning_content` collides with the client's echoed `reasoning` — 400 "duplicate field \`reasoning\`

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## TL;DR / 中文摘要

本地部署的 DeepSeek 引擎（serde 反序列化）把 `reasoning_content` 视为 `reasoning` 的同一字段（别名）。客户端（pi、dsh）会把它自己流式收到的思考以 `reasoning` 字段回传到历史消息里。而 magpie 对 host/model 含 "deepseek" 的 Chat 上游，在工具调用轮给这些消息**追加** `reasoning_content`（`withReasoningOnToolTurns`），却不删除原有的 `reasoning`。两条消息字段同现，服务端反序列化直接报：

```
400 {"code":"json_parse_error","message":"deepseek: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[6]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 70565","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}
```

结果：**只要走 magpie 且模型发起工具调用，紧随其后的每一条请求必 400**；不经 magpie 直连则一切正常。

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1307 (installed, Windows 11 x64); verified against source commit `b855cfee`
- Clients: `pi` (OpenAI Chat) and `dsh`; both process-local
- Upstream: **self-hosted local DeepSeek engine** ("DeepSeek-Flash", OpenAI Chat-compatible, host redacted; both `/v1/chat/completions`; endpoint types incl. openai/anthropic/responses)

## What happens

For a request relayed as Chat to an upstream whose host or model contains `deepseek` (`chatReplaysReasoning`), magpie adds `reasoning_content` to every assistant tool-call turn — and to the reply turns after tool results — via `withReasoningOnToolTurns` (`internal/gateway/chattidy.go`, called from the `provider.Chat` branch in `internal/gateway/gateway.go`).

The engine this client talks to **streams assistant thinking in `reasoning`** (not `reasoning_content`). The client therefore echoes earlier tool-call turns' thinking in `reasoning`. After magpie's injection those messages carry **both** fields, and the engine's serde rejects a message with both keys mapped to the same struct field:

```text
duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column …
```

Every request of such a turn fails, so the whole tool call loop breaks. Direct (no magpie) sends only one field and works.

## Behavior verified directly against the engine (bypassing magpie)

Same conversation, assistant turn with `tool_calls` + tool result, only the assistant fields differed:

| assistant message fields | result |
| --- | --- |
| `"reasoning": "…"` only | **200** |
| `"reasoning_content": "…"` only | **200** |
| both | **400** `duplicate field \`reasoning\`` (exact error above) |

## magpie-side evidence

While routing `pi` and `dsh` through magpie, magpie's own usage ledger shows the identical shape every time on this provider:

- `pi`: 200 (`stop: "tool_calls"`) → next request **400** (user-visible: `messages[9]`)
- `dsh`: 200 (`stop: "tool_calls"`) → next request **400**, retry **400** (user-visible: `messages[6]`)

All other turns (no tool call, `stop: "stop"`) succeed — they don't match `withReasoningOnToolTurns`' injection condition, so no field collision.

## Why I think it's on the magpie side

The replay rule exists because official API assumes a **DeepSeek-style upstream that wants `reasoning_content` back on tool turns**. This engine is a DeepSeek-model Chat API too, but it *names* the field `reasoning` (that's what it streams) and tolerates reading the thinking from either name alone — just not both at once. The injection therefore assumes the more common client shape (thinking absent, or echoed as `reasoning_content`) and leaves any client-echoed `reasoning` in place.

## Suggested fix (draft)

In `withReasoningOnToolTurns` (`internal/gateway/chattidy.go`), after taking the thinking text, **remove the fields it was taken from** before writing `reasoning_content`, so the thinking is carried exactly once:

```go
think := reasoningText(m)
if think == "" {
    think = noReasoning
}
// the thinking rode in `reasoning`/`reasoning_details`: they go, or an
// upstream that reads both into one field (`reasoning`, with
// `reasoning_content` an alias) takes the message apart instead
// ("duplicate field `reasoning`")
for _, f := range messageReasoning[1:] {
    delete(m, f)
}
m["reasoning_content"], _ = marshalPlain(think)
```

(And in the early-return branch where the message already has a non-empty `reasoning_content`, drop leftover `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` the same way, returning `true` when it changed.)

Note this is lossless for official-style upstreams: the thinking still reaches the model — just under the name they actually read — and a client that echoed thinking in `reasoning` stops producing a two-key message. Possibly the same collision exists on the Kimi path (`reasoningDetailsAsContent` keeps `reasoning` while adding `reasoning_content`); not checked.

## Related observation

A `codex` run routed to the same engine through `/v1/responses` also failed with 400s around the same time (a different shape — `input[…]-level errors, not this exact text). Didn't repro it; mentioning in case it's the same vector from the Responses side (`withReasoningText`).

## Workarounds tried

- No config switch found for the replay/injection (checked settings + providers).
- Renaming the model inside magpie (to a name without `deepseek`) risks breaking upstream model resolution; no alias mapping exists in `providers.json`.
- Removing the client's echoed `reasoning` client-side isn't configurable either (pi/dsh echo the field the engine itself streams).

So for now, bypassing magpie for this provider is the practical workaround.

issue.title: TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget is red on go1.27.3: turn 3 makes 19 of 30, one image fewer kept than the budget says

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
On go1.27.3 (linux/amd64, a WSL2 dev box), on current main, run calmly on
its own:

    go test -tags nogui -run 'TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget' ./internal/gateway/

is red:

    codex_images_test.go:362: turn 3 made 19 of 30 images, with 10 kept

(expected: turn 1 makes 30, later turns 20, 10 kept). The test builds its
budget from the size of one fitted image (10*one+one/2), so anything that
changes image/png's encoder output size between Go versions shifts the
boundary and keeps one image fewer. CI stays green on 1.26.x; a 1.27 box
gets this deterministically.

Not tried: pinning Go 1.26 on the same box to confirm the encoder drift, or
printing the fitted sizes per turn.

issue.title: [UI/UX] 长对话“Compact at”输入框缺乏防呆校验：若误输入纯数字 400 会被当作 400 tokens 导致下游客户端死循环 Compact 耗尽额度

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### 问题描述

在 Magpie 设置的「长对话（Compact at）」配置项中，右侧输入框要求输入诸如 `400k`、`272k` 这样带有单位的字符串。

如果用户直觉性地输入了纯数字（例如输入 `400`，误以为输入框单位默认是 k，或者习惯性直接输数字）：
- Magpie 会直接将其解析为 **400 tokens**，并在 `~/.config/magpie/settings.json` 中保存 `"compactAt": 400`。
- 随后 Magpie 同步生成的 `~/.codex/magpie-desktop-models.json` 会将下游所有路由组模型的 `context_window` 强制写入为 **400**。

### 造成的严重后果

1. **下游客户端死循环 Compact：**
   Codex 等客户端读取到的模型上下文上限仅有 400 tokens。而正常会话的 System Prompt 和工具调用（如 `read`、`pwd`）立刻会达到数千 tokens，导致**每执行一次命令或发一句话就强制触发一次 50~60 秒的 Context Compaction**（“一句一 compact”）。
2. **账号额度极速被耗尽：**
   因为不断在触发后台压缩总结请求，短短几分钟就会打满模型提供商的限流 / 5 小时配额（提示 `Heads up, you have less than 5% of your 5h limit left`）。

### 为什么当前交互设计不合理

1. **混杂单位输入极其反直觉：**
   常规界面的数字类配置输入框要么在右侧固定显示单位后缀（如 `k tokens`），框内仅允许纯数字；要么直接以完整 token 计（如输入 `400000`）。很少有直接让用户在文本框内自行键入 `400k` 混合格式的设计，极易引起误解和手误。
2. **缺乏防呆与范围校验（Sanity Check）：**
   对于现代 LLM 来说，几百 tokens 的上下文窗口在工程上毫无实用价值。当用户输入一个极小数值（如 `< 1000`）时，系统不仅没有拦截或警告，反而静默放行并持久化，直接导致下游瘫痪。

### 改进建议

1. **输入框形态优化（推荐）：**
   - 方式 A：输入框外置固定单位标签（如 `K tokens`），输入框改为纯数字输入（`type="number"`），用户填 `400` 时后台自动换算为 `400,000`。
   - 方式 B：或者直接以原生 token 数字为主，提供下拉推荐预设（272k / 400k / 1M / 自定义）。
2. **添加防呆提示与合理阈值校验：**
   - 在 `parseContexts` 或保存逻辑中增加范围检查：若用户输入的数值小于合理下限（如 `< 10000` 或用户输入的数值没有带单位且 `< 2000`），提示用户确认是否意为 `k tokens`，或给出格式错误警告，禁止直接将 `< 1000` 的微小数值写入全局 `compactAt`。

issue.title: gateway: a Responses reply to another agent carries events outside the Responses enum (`codex.*`, `response.metadata`, `keepalive`), and a typed client drops the whole turn

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

A turn through a ChatGPT Codex account dies before any of the reply is seen:

```
shell.turn.inference_failed  kind=serialization
serialization error: unknown variant `codex.rate_limits`, expected one of
`response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.completed`,
`response.failed`, `response.incomplete`, `response.output_item.added`, ...
```

Grok Build shows it as ``Couldn't read the response: serialization error: unknown variant `codex.rate_limits` … Try sending again.``, magpie's own request log has the turn as `499 the agent canceled the request`, and nothing retries: the client's typed event enum has no name for the event, so the whole turn is lost.

Filtering one such event only uncovers the next behind it: the same turn has since died on `unknown variant \`response.metadata\``, then on `unknown variant \`keepalive\``, and then on `serialization error: missing field \`created_at\``, which is magpie's own `response.failed` ending a stream the upstream cut short.

Seen with magpie 0.1.2284–0.1.2328 and Grok Build 1.0.45–1.0.70 (`xai-grok-sampler`, async-openai's `ResponseStreamEvent`), model `codex/gpt-6.1-terra` asked at `/v1/responses`.

## Repro

The backend's reply keeps the two events it tells only Codex by, and a client that is not Codex is handed them. `POST /v1/responses` with one of the ChatGPT models, as any OpenAI Responses client asks it:

```bash
curl -sS -N -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <magpie key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"codex/gpt-6.1-terra","stream":true,"input":"say OK"}' | grep '^event:'
```

What comes back (the first two lines are the problem):

```
event: codex.rate_limits
event: codex.response.metadata
event: response.created
event: response.in_progress
...
event: response.completed
```

It is intermittent on this route: the same body asked at 00:59 and 01:03 came back with no `codex.*` event at all, and every ask from 01:12 on carried both. `response.metadata` arrives in the middle of a reply, `keepalive` only when the upstream is quiet, and the `response.failed` body appears only when a stream is cut mid-reply — so a client loses some turns and not others, which reads as a flaky upstream rather than a shape problem.

## Why

`passthrough` relays whatever the ChatGPT backend writes. Part of it is the Codex protocol, not the OpenAI Responses API: `codex.rate_limits` and `codex.response.metadata` (the account's windows, the model list's tag), `response.metadata` (the turn's state on a socket, its moderation word on the HTTP route), and a `keepalive` event a quiet upstream sends. A Responses client with a closed event enum — Grok Build's async-openai `ResponseStreamEvent` — reads one of those and ends the turn before the reply: `unknown variant \`codex.rate_limits\``, then `unknown variant \`response.metadata\``, then `unknown variant \`keepalive\``.

The same boundary has a second failure shape. When the upstream stream dies mid-reply, `passthrough` ends it with its own `response.failed` (`streamFailure` in `gateway.go`), which carried only `{"object","status","error"}`. The name is legal, but a typed client reads that `response` into a full `Response` whose `id`, `object`, `created_at`, `model`, `output` and `status` are required, so the turn died on `serialization error: missing field \`created_at\`` — hiding the cut-from-upstream failure behind a parse error, non-retryable.

## Fix

Branch on my fork, rebased on `80ccaba64`: `crayonlu/magpie@codex-lead-events` — https://github.com/crayonlu/magpie/tree/codex-lead-events. PRs here are for collaborators, so the branch rides in this issue.

`internal/gateway/responses_enum.go` holds the OpenAI Responses event enum as a set and a `responsesEnumTidy` that drops every whole SSE frame whose `event:` name (or, where the stream names none, the data's `type`) is not in it. It runs last in `passthrough`'s filter chain, only for `proto == provider.Responses && sse` and only when the client is not Codex — `!fromCodex(r.Header) && agentOf(r) != "codex"`, the pair `codex_own_v1.go` already uses. Codex's own request keeps every event as the backend sent it. The quota tap (`codexLimitsTap`) and failover's `sniff` read the upstream bytes before the filter, so limit accounting and classification are untouched.

`streamFailure` now builds a whole `Response` for `response.failed` (`id`, `object`, `created_at`, `status`, `model`, `output`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `tool_choice`, `tools`, `error`) and carries the stream's next `sequence_number`: `responses_seq.go` watches the last one that went out, so the added event continues the numbering the client reads.

The socket route carries the same guard now: `socketTurnWriter.headerFrames()` returns nothing for a client that isn't Codex, so the `response.metadata` / `codex.response.metadata` / `codex.rate_limits` it synthesizes from the reply's headers no longer reach a foreign typed client on the WebSocket (`responses_ws.go`).

`internal/gateway/responses_enum_test.go` drives the real `/v1/responses` passthrough against a fixture ChatGPT sign-in, one turn with no `User-Agent`, `xai-grok-shell/1.0.45`, `codex_cli_rs/0.166.0`, and `magpie-codex` (a key owned by the codex agent). The first two must get only enum events; the last two must keep `codex.rate_limits`, `codex.response.metadata`, `response.metadata` and `keepalive`. `TestResponsesEnumAllowed` covers the predicate on its own. `TestPassthroughResponsesEndsShort` now asserts the cut-stream `response.failed` carries the full response.

## What was run

macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, temp `HOME`.

- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run 'TestResponsesEventsOutsideTheEnumStayWithCodex|TestResponsesEnumAllowed|TestPassthroughResponsesEndsShort' -count=1` — passes at `85e37162e`. With the predicate forced to `true` the same test fails and prints the leaked frames: `event codex.rate_limits there=true`, `event response.metadata there=true`, `event keepalive there=true, want false`. `TestResponsesEnumAllowed` passes under `-race -count=20`.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -count=1` — 2 reds on this machine, the same 2 on the unpatched tree at `80ccaba64`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `TestMarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal` (#3547, Go 1.27 leaves U+2028/U+2029 unescaped where `encoding/json` does not). No new red.
- `TestResponsesEventsAreClientShaped` walks a translated reply and fails any event without `sequence_number`, or any `response` without `id/object/created_at/status/model/output` — the guard against the next missing field, added after the client reported `missing field sequence_number`.
- `gofmt -l internal/gateway` clean; `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` and `go build ./...` clean, apart from the darwin cgo deprecation warnings `main` prints.
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` at an earlier base of this branch (`4182e68`): 79 packages ok; the only reds were the same gateway environment ones above plus `internal/plugin`'s `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207, Bun 1.4.4 here against a test pinned to 1.4.2).
- Against the running gateway: a build of this branch was installed and driven with `curl`. A non-Codex `User-Agent` got `response.created … response.completed` with none of `codex.*`, `response.metadata` or `keepalive`; `codex_cli_rs` got all of them. The `response.failed` shape was reproduced from a client log (`serialization error: missing field \`created_at\``) and pinned to `streamFailure`.
- `make test-ui` — not run; no GUI file or asset is touched.

issue.title: [Bug] 网关在 key 已报限额用尽后仍先发请求，Gemini 按天额度用完后整天反复被拒（已定位，附修复分支）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
起因是想让网关在发出请求之前就知道某个 key 已经用不了，而不是先发过去、等几秒拿到 429 再切下一个成员。先核对了两家官方文档，结论是“查询余额”这条路走不通，但有两处可以提前判断的信号 Magpie 目前没有用上。

## 背景：OpenAI / Gemini 的 key 能拿到什么

- **OpenAI**：普通 key 没有余额接口（Usage / Costs API 据社区说法需要 admin key，官方页面 403，未能核实）。响应可以带 `x-ratelimit-limit-*`、`x-ratelimit-remaining-requests|tokens|project-tokens`，以及 `x-ratelimit-reset-*`，后者是一段时长，示例为 `6m0s`、`1s`（[Rate limits 指南](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)：“Responses can include the following header fields”）。限额按模型计，部分模型族共享。
- **Anthropic** 的 API key 带 `anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,output-tokens}-remaining`，以及 RFC 3339 格式的对应 `-reset`（[Rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)）。
- **Gemini API**：没有任何接口或响应头报告剩余额度。限额按 project 计（RPM / TPM / RPD），RPD 在太平洋时间午夜重置，只能在 AI Studio 查看用量（[Rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits)）。

所以能做的“预估”是两件事：OpenAI/Anthropic 用成功响应里的 remaining 头；Gemini 用 429 正文里的 quotaId 推算重置时间。

## Magpie 现在的行为

1. **成功响应里的 remaining 头没人读。** `restAfter` 只在 ≥400 时读 `Retry-After` / `x-ratelimit-reset-*`。一个 key 回 200 且 `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 0` 时，下一个请求仍然先发给它，吃一个 429 才切换。而且成功路径上的 `hw.header` 只有 `PassedReplyHeaders`（默认只有 request id），即使想在 `servedCandidate` 之后读，也读不到这些头。
2. **Gemini 按天的额度用完后，会整天被反复请求。** Gemini 的 PerDay 429 正文里写着 “Please retry in 33.517s”，RetryInfo 是 `33s`。`resetsAt` 会先读到这个时间，于是 key 只休息约 33 秒（没有这句时则是 `quotaRest` 的 15 分钟）。这个提示说的不是当天额度，额度要到太平洋时间午夜才恢复，所以这个 key 会整天“恢复→被拒→再休息”。`auto/<model>` 组里排在第一的 Gemini key 会让后续每个请求都先失败一次。

## 参考实现

- [分支 `fix/rest-before-rate-limit`](https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/tree/fix/rest-before-rate-limit)
- [提交 3dc7dec6](https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/commit/3dc7dec61fc9a84d75c220b560a385516912721e)
- [对比](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...hhh2210:magpie:fix/rest-before-rate-limit)

改动内容：

- **成功响应带 remaining=0 时提前休息**（`spentRest` / `restIfSpent`，在 `servedCandidate` 之后调用）。OpenAI 的 `x-ratelimit-remaining-*` 或 Anthropic 的 `anthropic-ratelimit-*-remaining` 为 `0`、且对应的 reset 头可以解析时，这个 key 的该模型（`restID`，因为 OpenAI 按模型计；共享限额的模型族要等各自撞到才会休息）休息到 reset，最长 `longestWait`。原始头通过 reply sink 旁路保存（`withLimitSink` → `holdWriter.heardLimits`），不改变转发给 agent 的头；System One 的 decide 路径直接用 `postDecide` 返回的头。只读 OpenAI（api.openai.com）和 Anthropic（api.anthropic.com）官方 API 的各自响应头；中转站转发上游 key 的头时不读，因为那是它某个上游 key 的状态，不代表中转站本身。订阅账号（`Account != nil`）、Anthropic 的 `unified` 头、`LimitRestOff` 的 provider 不受影响。
- **Gemini PerDay 额度休息到太平洋时间午夜**（`geminiDayBackIn`）。仅对 `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` 生效，在 `resetsAt` 之前判断。用户自己设置的 `QuotaResetAt` / `OwnQuotaRest` 仍然优先。其他 host 的同样正文、以及 Gemini PerMinute 额度保持原样。
- `retryAfter` 的三种时间格式解析抽成 `resetIn`，两处共用。
- 同步更新了 `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md` 的两条规则。

生产代码 +166/-9，测试 +190/-0，文档 +2。

## 验证

- `TestSpentLimitRestsBeforeRefusal`（json / stream）：provider 指向 api.openai.com，`s.client` 重定向到 httptest 上游；上游给第一个 key 回 200 + `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Requests: 0` / `X-Ratelimit-Reset-Requests: 6m0s`，经完整 `Server.Handler()` 发两次请求。修复后第二次直接落到另一个 key，并且该 key 的模型休息 6 分钟。把成功路径改回读 `hw.header` 后，测试失败：`asked map[k-spent:2]`。
- `TestSpentRest`：OpenAI 的 requests/tokens（取较长者）、Anthropic 的 RFC 3339 reset、有剩余、无 reset、unified、订阅账号、`LimitRestOff`、中转站、两家的头互相出现在对方 host 上；同时断言休息的 key 是 `restID`。去掉 host 限定后，`relay`、`anthropic's from openai`、`openai's from anthropic` 三项失败。
- `TestGeminiDayQuotaRestsUntilMidnightPacific`：用仓库里已有的真实 PerDay 429 正文（含 33s RetryInfo）。去掉 `geminiDayBackIn`，或把它放在 `resetsAt` 之后（我第一版就是这么写的），测试都会失败：只休息约 33 秒。另外覆盖用户 `QuotaResetAt` 优先、非 Google host 不变、PerMinute 仍按速率限制处理。在 `TZ=UTC`、`Pacific/Kiritimati`、`America/Los_Angeles` 下都跑过。
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8`（`go.mod` 的版本）下 `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` 整包通过（504s）。
- `gofmt -l` 无新增（`internal/library/skillgit_test.go` 在上游原本就有）；macOS、Linux nogui、Windows 的 `go vet ./internal/gateway` 和 `go build ./...` 均通过。
- 完整 `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`（Go 1.27.3，沙盒 HOME，基于 `03f609e3f`）：78 个包通过。8 个失败用例在干净的 `03f609e3f` 上单独复跑同样失败，且都已有 issue：`TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` / `FuzzMarshalRaw`（#3547，Go 1.27）、`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`（#3680，Go 1.27）、`TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget`（#3045）、`TestSettingsSaveKeepsWhatItDoesNotSend`（#4514）、`TestPluginSOCKSProxy`（#2207）、`TestNoCommandBypassesProc`（#4491）、`TestColdTurnsTaken`（#4510，`-count=5` 第一轮失败后挂起，和 #4510 中描述的一致）。
- 未做真实使用验收：没有用真实 OpenAI key 观察 remaining 归零，也没有用真实 Gemini key 撞当天额度。

## 未覆盖 / 可以后续做

- askJev 路径（`decide_group.go` 的 `servedCandidate(c, 0)`）拿不到响应头，没有覆盖。embeddings 的 `heardHeaders` sink 没接 limit sink。
- Gemini 没有 remaining 头，所以第一次 429 仍然要实际发出去；改动只是让之后整天不再重复踩。
- 更进一步的“发送前预估”（用 `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` 对比本次请求的 token 估算，不够就跳过）没有做：remaining 只是上一次响应时的快照，并发下会偏乐观，判断阈值需要维护者决定。

了解到仓库不接受外部 PR，所以把问题和参考实现放在这里，供维护者或维护 agent 复现和评估；分支可以直接 cherry-pick，也可以只作参考重新实现。

@yetone 方便时请看一下。

issue.title: gateway: slow request-body uploads hit pre-routing 504 with misleading retry/restart guidance (0.1.1255)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A long Pi conversation repeatedly received `504: magpie held this request for 2m0s without routing it to any provider` through a Remote Magpie connection. The remote gateway's watchdog dump showed handlers waiting for TLS request-body bytes in `readSized`, before provider selection. Switching from an automatic routing group to an explicit Codex route produced the same failure.

Compacting the conversation and restoring the original automatic route recovered the session: a bounded probe returned `ROUTE_OK` in approximately 7 seconds. The error's recommendation to resend or restart Magpie was misleading for this case; resending the same large context repeatedly encountered the same upload bottleneck.

## Environment and scope

- Client: Pi running on macOS, through a local Magpie gateway.
- Transport: local Magpie → remote Magpie over HTTPS on a slow international/private-network connection.
- Remote gateway: **0.1.1255**, Linux, running as a user service. The serving executable path was checked, rather than relying on a potentially different CLI on PATH.
- Endpoints seen in the remote logs: `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`.
- The automatic group used `routing=smart`, `stays=auto`, with Codex and TRAE members serving the same GPT model.
- **Not reproduced on the current latest release.** At filing time GitHub reports `v0.1.2597`. This report describes the deployed version above; it does not establish that the behavior remains in the latest version.

## Observed behavior

The client repeatedly received:

```text
Singapore Magpie: magpie held this request for 2m0s without routing it to any provider,
so it was stopped rather than left waiting. Send it again; if it keeps happening,
restart magpie and report it with magpie's log, which says where it was held.
(504: you can retry your request)
```

A representative server log was:

```text
gateway: POST /v1/responses for ? from pi held 2m0s before routing,
not masking it; stopped with 504; where every goroutine stood:
```

Relevant frames from the watchdog dump (unrelated goroutines omitted):

```text
internal/poll.runtime_pollWait
internal/poll.(*FD).Read
net.(*conn).Read
crypto/tls.(*Conn).readRecordOrCCS
crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read
net/http.(*connReader).Read
net/http.(*body).readLocked
net/http.(*body).Read
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.waitedBody.Read
    internal/gateway/unrouted.go:400
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.(*idleBody).Read
    internal/gateway/request_bounds.go:65
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.readSized
    internal/gateway/request_bounds.go:240
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.readBoundedRequestBody
    internal/gateway/request_bounds.go:191
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.(*Server).readRequestBody
    internal/gateway/request_bounds.go:47
github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway.(*Server).requestBody
    internal/gateway/request_bounds.go:39
```

## Checks and recovery

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Small fresh requests through the automatic group and explicit Codex route | Both returned HTTP 200 in approximately 4 seconds |
| Original long conversation switched to explicit Codex route | Same remote pre-routing 504 |
| Independent synthetic 1 MB request uploaded directly to the remote HTTPS gateway | 1,000,090 bytes uploaded in 18.72 seconds, approximately 53 KB/s; received the expected unknown-model 404 after body parsing |
| Synthetic 20 MB request uploaded directly to the remote HTTPS gateway, with a 40-second client cutoff | Only 1,769,472 bytes uploaded in 40 seconds, approximately 44 KB/s; curl timed out (the measurement ran alongside a local-forwarding probe) |
| Two native Pi compactions, then restore the original automatic group | Same conversation returned `ROUTE_OK` in approximately 7 seconds; normal completion, no tool calls |

The retained transcript suffix was approximately 23.4 MB before recovery, including substantial image data, and approximately 5.3 MB after the two compactions. **These are serialized transcript measurements, not captured HTTP Content-Length values.** Raw history remained intact; compaction appended checkpoints and reduced the context sent on subsequent turns.

The evidence supports a request-body transfer bottleneck preceding routing. The underlying reason for the low network throughput is not established, and the dump alone does not distinguish continuous slow progress from pauses between reads. No routing-group policy change or shared gateway restart was needed to recover this conversation.

## Suggested reproduction

This is a synthetic reproducer for maintainers to try; the exact throttled command below has **not** been run as a full end-to-end reproduction. The measurements above used the naturally slow connection.

1. Run an HTTPS Magpie gateway with a gateway key.
2. Generate a large JSON body. An intentionally unknown model avoids an upstream inference call while still exercising body parsing:

   ```bash
   python3 - <<'PY'
   import json
   with open('/tmp/magpie-slow-body.json', 'w') as f:
       json.dump({
           'model': 'route-diagnostic-invalid-model',
           'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'x' * 20_000_000}],
       }, f)
   PY
   ```

3. Upload it at a controlled slow rate, using a gateway URL and key supplied through environment variables:

   ```bash
   curl --silent --show-error \
     --limit-rate 50k --max-time 180 \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAGPIE_GATEWAY_KEY" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data-binary @/tmp/magpie-slow-body.json \
     "$MAGPIE_BASE_URL/chat/completions" \
     -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code} uploaded=%{size_upload} seconds=%{time_total}\n'
   ```

4. Inspect whether the unrouted watchdog aborts the upload around two minutes, which read stage it reports, and whether a progressing upload is distinguished from an idle or stalled body.

## Expected behavior / possible improvements

- Distinguish request-body upload waits from provider-selection waits in the client-facing error and diagnostic report.
- Report bytes received / expected, elapsed upload time, and last-progress age where available. This would make the reason actionable without interpreting a full goroutine dump.
- If an absolute upload limit intentionally terminates the request, explain that limit and suggest reducing/compacting the request or checking the connection. Resending unchanged data or restarting the gateway should not be the primary guidance for this condition.
- Check that the body idle timeout and the unrouted watchdog interact as intended for uploads that continue making progress. A regression test could cover a progressing upload that outlasts the unrouted budget, while retaining protection against genuinely stalled clients.

## Related reports

- #4602: similar client-facing pre-routing 504 wording; this report adds body-read stacks and transfer measurements.
- #2567 and #4511: request-body progress / timeout classification tests.
- #4766: a long Pi session also fails before routing, but its reported bottleneck is masking after the body has been read. The observed wait here is in TLS/body reads.

No conversation contents, images, credentials, internal addresses, or full diagnostic dumps are included.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex /models：x-api-key 覆盖有效 OAuth 为 Bearer magpie，导致 401 和上下文回退

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 问题与影响

Codex 保留 ChatGPT 登录、同时使用 Magpie 的 managed gateway key 时，GET `/backend-api/codex/models` 会返回 401。已用同一份有效 OAuth 做请求对照：只去掉 `x-api-key`，同一路径立即返回 200 和正确的模型窗口。

源码确认：`identifyCaller` 验证 gateway key 后，把原本有效的 `Authorization` 覆盖为内部标记 `Bearer magpie`；模型目录路径随后把这个标记转发给 ChatGPT，没有重新签名。

这会让 Codex 无法刷新 Magpie 声明的模型元数据。本机 Astra 会话的有效窗口实际从 828400 回退到 258400，自动压缩阈值从 784800 降到 244800，长会话随后反复压缩。模型和推理档位仍为 Astra / Ultra。

## 环境与配置

- Magpie **v0.1.2909**，macOS arm64。
- Codex 桌面端内置 CLI **0.166.0-alpha.6**。
- 核查时间：2026-11-04。
- Magpie 的 Codex provider 对 `gpt-6-astra` 显式设置 `contexts = 872000`。
- Codex 没有显式设置 `model_context_window` 或 `model_auto_compact_token_limit`。
- 当前接入配置如下；不主张这段配置一定由 Magpie 自动生成：

```toml
model = "gpt-6-astra"
model_provider = "custom"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"

[model_providers.custom]
name = "OpenAI"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
supports_websockets = false

[model_providers.custom.http_headers]
x-api-key = "<valid Magpie managed gateway key>"
```

该 custom provider 没有 `experimental_bearer_token`，也没有额外配置 `Authorization`；OAuth 来自 Codex 已有登录。

## 最小复现：仅查询模型目录

对同一个本机网关发送：

```http
GET /backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.166.0
Authorization: Bearer <valid Codex OAuth access token>
ChatGPT-Account-ID: <matching account>
x-api-key: <valid Magpie managed gateway key>
Accept: application/json
```

在同一次验证中，仅改变认证头组合：

| 请求头 | 实际结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 有效 OAuth + 对应 account header + 有效 x-api-key | **401** |
| 同一份 OAuth + 同一个 account header，去掉 x-api-key | **200**；Astra 的 context_window 和 max_context_window 均为 **872000** |
| 只有有效 x-api-key | **401**，错误相同 |

401 正文：

```json
{"detail":"Could not parse your authentication token. Please try signing in again."}
```

第二组仍然经过 Magpie，并非绕开网关直连。它说明这一失败不需要 OAuth 失效或重新登录才能触发。验证只发送 GET 模型目录请求，没有为此发送推理请求。

## 源码原因

以下链接固定到安装版本 v0.1.2909：

1. [loopback 请求带 managed key 时进入 identifyCaller](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L493-L503)；[callerKeys / managedKey 包含 x-api-key](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L740-L774)。
2. [identifyCaller 无条件覆盖 Authorization](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L672-L680)：

   ```go
   r.Header = r.Header.Clone()
   r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+Token)
   ```

   [Token 是公开常量 "magpie"](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/gateway.go#L54)，不是用户的 OAuth。
3. [GET /models 进入 codexModels](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L90-L93)。[askCodexList 复制认证头后直接发送](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2191-L2206)，[copyHeaders 保留 Authorization](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2073-L2078)。
4. [普通 401 原样返回，提前退出](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2225-L2251)，因此后续 [CodexNativeWindow / 窗口覆盖](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2279-L2294) 没有执行。

核查时 main 为 `3eb2bda4f2e3ba8aa0eb2c7870d9c746798687a1`；上述 `lan.go` 和 `codex_backend.go` 与 v0.1.2909 完整文件内容一致。运行复现基于安装版，main 只做了源码对照。

## 上下文回退的现场证据

同一个 Astra / Ultra 长会话在当天 15:23 前后出现以下运行时值变化（UTC+8，摘录必要字段）：

```text
full_context_window_limit: 828400 -> 258400
auto_compact_scope_limit: 784800 -> 244800
```

Codex 当前安装程序的内置 Astra 目录是 `context_window=272000, max_context_window=872000`；258400 正好是 `272000 × 95%`。正常拿到 Magpie 的 872000 覆盖时，有效窗口为 828400。

同机还出现过缓存过期和 provider/auth identity mismatch，但不是每条都来自受影响会话的进程；不把它们当成这次认证覆盖的必要触发条件，也没有把每次历史窗口跳变都归因于同一原因。

## 期望

同时携带有效 gateway key 和 ChatGPT OAuth 时，gateway key 用于本地身份/权限校验，Codex 原生目录请求应保留或正确恢复其上游 OAuth 身份，不能把内部 `Bearer magpie` 发给 ChatGPT。

建议增加回归用例：在 mock ChatGPT 上游断言“有效 OAuth + managed x-api-key”的模型目录请求仍使用正确 OAuth，且返回列表应用用户的窗口覆盖；同时保留 gateway key 的权限和失效检查。

相关：#1955 是模型目录超时后的旧窗口回退；#4308 是登录确已被撤销。本例的区别是 OAuth 本身有效，加上 managed x-api-key 才触发 401。


另见 #2145：该报告针对 WSL NAT 的远程接入，维护者通过调整接入方式修复且报告者已确认。本例发生在本机回环地址，并用有效 OAuth 与 managed key 的双凭据对照定位到了头部覆盖。
